question: Why is the baby's head often considered the trickiest part during a normal delivery?

options.A: It is the largest and least compressible part
options.B: It lacks any protective bony covering
options.C: It is heavier than the rest of the body
options.D: It remains completely rigid throughout labour

explanation: You've got this! Because the skull is large and made of firm bone, getting it safely through the narrow pelvis is the biggest physical challenge during birth. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T10#GNS121_U6_T10_h1)

question: Why is it a good thing that a newborn baby's skull bones aren't completely fused together yet?

options.A: It allows the bones to overlap during passage
options.B: It makes the baby's head completely round
options.C: It speeds up the overall growth of the baby
options.D: It prevents any blood flow to the brain

explanation: Brilliant! Those movable bones can slightly overlap (moulding), which helps the baby's head squeeze through the birth canal safely. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T10#GNS121_U6_T10_h1)

question: Which bones make up the large upper sides and roof of a baby's skull?
explanation: Spot on! The two parietal bones form the main large areas on the sides and top of the baby's head vault. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T10#GNS121_U6_T10_h2)

question: Where is the occipital bone located on a baby's skull?

options.A: Inside the centre of the brain
options.B: At the very front of the forehead
options.C: On the lower side near the ear
options.D: At the back of the head

explanation: You nailed it! The occipital bone forms the lower back part and base of the skull. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T10#GNS121_U6_T10_h2)

question: Which suture runs right down the middle, separating the two parietal bones?
explanation: Great job! The sagittal suture lies right along the midline between the left and right parietal bones. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T10#GNS121_U6_T10_h3)

question: During a vaginal examination in labour, why do midwives feel for the baby's skull sutures?

options.A: To check the amount of amniotic fluid remaining
options.B: To measure the exact weight of the unborn baby
options.C: To listen to the foetal heart rate more clearly
options.D: To determine the exact position of the foetal head

explanation: Well done! Feeling the sutures helps you figure out which way the baby is facing and how well labour is progressing. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T10#GNS121_U6_T10_h3)

question: What shape is the anterior fontanelle (the larger soft spot)?
explanation: You got it! The anterior fontanelle where four bones meet is famously diamond-shaped. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T10#GNS121_U6_T10_h4)

question: If you notice a baby's anterior fontanelle is bulging outwards, what might this tell you?
explanation: Keep it up! Extra pressure inside the skull pushes the soft membrane outward, causing that noticeable bulge. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T10#GNS121_U6_T10_h4)

question: In a normal, smooth delivery, what part of the baby's head usually comes out first?
explanation: Awesome! The vertex is the ideal presenting part because it lets the smallest head measurements pass through the pelvis first. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T10#GNS121_U6_T10_h5)

question: Which area of the baby's head sits right between the bridge of the nose and the front soft spot?
explanation: Spot on! The brow (or synciput) is the area right above the eyes up to the front fontanelle. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T10#GNS121_U6_T10_h5)

question: When the baby's head is nicely tucked down to its chest, what is the measurement of the smallest head diameter (suboccipito-bregmatic)?
explanation: You're doing great! A fully tucked head presents the suboccipito-bregmatic diameter, which is a cozy 9.5 cm. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T10#GNS121_U6_T10_h6)

question: A mother's labour is taking longer because the baby's head is tilted back, presenting the longest measurement. Which diameter is causing this delay?
explanation: Clinical thinking! The mento-vertical diameter is the largest at 13.5 cm (seen in a brow presentation), which makes sliding through the pelvis tough work. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T10#GNS121_U6_T10_h6)

question: What is the main reason a baby's skull undergoes moulding during labour?

options.A: To close all fontanelles before birth
options.B: To reduce head dimensions to fit the pelvis
options.C: To speed up the heart rate of the mother
options.D: To increase the total brain volume of the baby

explanation: Brilliant! Moulding helps the head temporarily adjust its shape to smoothly navigate the curves of the birth canal. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T10#GNS121_U6_T10_h7)

question: What is a major risk if a baby's skull undergoes moulding too fast or too forcefully?

options.C: Complete closure of the sagittal suture

explanation: Spot on. While some moulding is normal, sudden and severe pressure can stress or tear delicate blood vessels inside the baby's head. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T10#GNS121_U6_T10_h7)
